# SAME and SAME R actual dataset audit

## Which original files were accessible?

### Takeaway
Both investigations are publicly accessible through the PSI API. The official combined analyzed workbook is the practical harmonized data source; the SAME experimental CSV is a plan, whereas SAME-R's CSV is an observed run/aging index. Metadata calls and downloads were executed successfully locally.

### Cited Findings
- Metadata endpoint is `https://psi.nasa.gov/geode-py/ws/repo/investigations/PSI-102` (and PSI-101). Both responses report investigation version 4, CC0-1.0. Saved unmodified JSONs under `data/raw/PSI-102-metadata.json` and `PSI-101-metadata.json`. The PSI-102 added-file list has 104 entries, including legacy `.xls` run time series, `.xlsx` logs, engineering documents, presentations and videos; PSI-101 includes analyzed run spreadsheets, HKP CSV time series, TEM images, videos, reports, and a combined workbook. Total file sizes reported by the metadata are 657608178 bytes for PSI-102 and 6308124750 for PSI-101, not downloaded totals. — [SAME metadata](https://psi.nasa.gov/geode-py/ws/repo/investigations/PSI-102); [SAME-R metadata](https://psi.nasa.gov/geode-py/ws/repo/investigations/PSI-101)
- Download resolution used `GET https://psi.nasa.gov/geode-py/ws/studies/PSI-101/download?file=PSI-101_Analyzed%20Data_SAME%2C%20SAME-R_Results.xlsx&version=4&redirect=false`. The response body is a plain signed URL (not JSON), fetched in a second GET. Temporary signed URL credentials must not be recorded as durable provenance. File metadata version is 1, investigation version is 4. Downloaded workbook has 4061669 bytes, SHA256 `6d3a539ccf425b1fa8edc19cc75d828f57d650c7ce734d4e7aa686fea9593218`. — [Official workbook resolver](https://psi.nasa.gov/geode-py/ws/studies/PSI-101/download?file=PSI-101_Analyzed%20Data_SAME%2C%20SAME-R_Results.xlsx&version=4&redirect=false)
- Downloaded SAME experimental table is 331 bytes SHA256 `268d1e121d2f211b124407dd32b9475617bd269ede2c2d1749441da3e949a2af`. It has eight numbered planned rows with Teflon conditions, followed by materials described as having the same conditions. It is not 8 observed independent experiments. SAME-R experimental table is 5674 bytes SHA256 `87164b7dc9168a4273c159f7a9f23699afbd06ad97b77974377e79b9bf8a3bef`, with actual run and aging identifiers and controls. — [SAME resolver](https://psi.nasa.gov/geode-py/ws/studies/PSI-102/download?file=PSI-102_Experimental%20table_SAME.csv&version=4&redirect=false); [SAME-R resolver](https://psi.nasa.gov/geode-py/ws/studies/PSI-101/download?file=PSI-101_Experimental%20table_SAME-R.csv&version=4&redirect=false)
- Downloaded `PSI-101_Reports_SAME-R_Final Report.pdf` has 4578437 bytes SHA256 `65381e2715eb7379113dd1b9c550baaa5fa5a247dba00419123143aa98ef80d6`; PDF metadata title is Microsoft Word - SAMER_Final 0602 2014.docx, 89 PDF pages, creation June 2 2014. `PSI-102_Reports_SAME_Final Science Report.pdf` has 3712845 bytes SHA256 `af91c96d22d93bbefbc0f2c5e1cc06e24813f532e5379b3fec9f121cccb22193`. — [SAME-R resolver](https://psi.nasa.gov/geode-py/ws/studies/PSI-101/download?file=PSI-101_Reports_SAME-R_Final%20Report.pdf&version=4&redirect=false); [SAME resolver](https://psi.nasa.gov/geode-py/ws/studies/PSI-102/download?file=PSI-102_Reports_SAME_Final%20Science%20Report.pdf&version=4&redirect=false)
- Public S3 bucket root listing was executed; only `DSI/`, `OASIS/`, `pk4/`, `index.html` are present. Prefix PSI-102 returns no keys. Therefore this mirror is not a viable SAME download route. Bare `/ws/studies/PSI-102` returned a permission message; this is an incorrect metadata route, not evidence the investigation is restricted. — [S3 listing](https://nasa-psi.s3.amazonaws.com/?list-type=2&delimiter=/)

### Inferences
- Prefer the official workbook's combined source-reduced data to reconstructing every instrument calibration from raw engineering time series on the hackathon timescale. Preserve source-reported calibrated quantities and avoid applying calibration twice.

### Gaps
- All time-series files and images were inventoried, not downloaded or decoded. No claim is made about time-series reading counts or complete raw-run coverage.

## How many independent units and what controls exist?

### Takeaway
The verified SAME-R count is 67 heating runs, not 66, with 109 records after secondary-aging measurements. The combined analyzed workbook covers a reduced subset of SAME. Row-level splitting would leak aging/reused-sample information.

### Cited Findings
- SAME-R report PDF page 3, Flight Operation, explicitly says 67 runs including two runs using reused samples and 109 when secondary aging is listed separately; 70 TEM samples collected. Flight July 16–September 9 2010. The report lists preloaded carousels plus 30 loose samples and says a Pyrell sample in carousel 5 position 6 was unusable. — [SAME-R report](https://psi.nasa.gov/geode-py/ws/studies/PSI-101/download?file=PSI-101_Reports_SAME-R_Final%20Report.pdf&version=4&redirect=false)
- `Combined Rslts Copy this sheet` worksheet (XLSX sheet22), row2 headers, has 154 recognized campaign rows: SAME 45, SAME-R 109. SAME 45 rows = 29 numerical heating identifiers with secondary suffix `a`; 20 rows/12 heating IDs are DBP calibration aerosol, leaving 25 material-smoke rows/17 heating runs. SAME-R has 67 numerical heating IDs48–114, plus42 suffix-a rows. SAME-R material rows: Kapton30, Silicone22, Lampwick20, Pyrell20, Teflon17. These counts were computed from actual cached workbook XML, extracted with stdlib zipfile+ElementTree and saved to `data/raw/workbook_sheet22_audit.json`. — [Official workbook](https://psi.nasa.gov/geode-py/ws/studies/PSI-101/download?file=PSI-101_Analyzed%20Data_SAME%2C%20SAME-R_Results.xlsx&version=4&redirect=false)
- SAME-R has65 distinct sample IDs among67 primary runs: L14 reused in54/57 (description57 explicitly reburn), K08 reused85/90 (90 explicitly reburn85). All109 rows have65 IDs, but51a lists K02 while51 lists K01, and61/61a list K02: group conservatively by graph connecting numerical run and any common sample ID, or exclude secondary-aging rows for the primary prediction task. With all109 rows this creates64 connected sample/run groups. Primary67 runs have65 physical sample groups. SAME primary nonDBP17 rows have17 unique carousel/position pairs; sample-ID column absent. — [Official workbook](https://psi.nasa.gov/geode-py/ws/studies/PSI-101/download?file=PSI-101_Analyzed%20Data_SAME%2C%20SAME-R_Results.xlsx&version=4&redirect=false)
- Controls in combined sheet: N inlet velocity cm/s, O Rt/R0 dimensionless setpoint, P heating duration s, Q primary-aging duration s, R primary-mixing duration s. U is net aging, often outcome-of-timing derived; do not assume it is a programmed independent control. SAME primary control ranges N2–8, O1.245–1.48, P10–60,Q8–720,R0–8; SAME-R N0–8.1,O1.22–1.48,P60–120,Q1–720,R8. All are finite in the17+67 nonDBP primary rows. — [Official workbook](https://psi.nasa.gov/geode-py/ws/studies/PSI-101/download?file=PSI-101_Analyzed%20Data_SAME%2C%20SAME-R_Results.xlsx&version=4&redirect=false)
- SAME-R report PDF pages2–3 says sample temperature was derived from logged engineering data, and the same Rt/R0 can produce different sample temperatures. Therefore Rt/R0 is a valid controlled predictor but is an imperfect physical surrogate for temperature. — [SAME-R report](https://psi.nasa.gov/geode-py/ws/studies/PSI-101/download?file=PSI-101_Reports_SAME-R_Final%20Report.pdf&version=4&redirect=false)
- Heating duration alone does not identify primary rows: SAME29a/41a/46a/47a retain positive P and51a in SAME-R retains P60, while many other secondary rows have P0. Explicit suffix filtering is needed. SAME flags L fan problem and M flat profiles are `n` for45 rows; SAME-R cells blank, so their absence is unknown, not a documented negative. SAME-R report PDF page3 says hardware worked fine overall. — [Workbook](https://psi.nasa.gov/geode-py/ws/studies/PSI-101/download?file=PSI-101_Analyzed%20Data_SAME%2C%20SAME-R_Results.xlsx&version=4&redirect=false); [Report](https://psi.nasa.gov/geode-py/ws/studies/PSI-101/download?file=PSI-101_Reports_SAME-R_Final%20Report.pdf&version=4&redirect=false)

### Inferences
- Use primary heating rows only for condition→ISS threshold-response learning; retain secondary rows for descriptive aging display. Group primary repeated physical sample IDs within campaign; SAME uses carousel/position fallback.
- The84 primary nonDBP rows represent82 conservative sample groups (17 SAME+65 SAME-R). Claims are limited to the analyzed subset, not every original SAME flight test.

### Gaps
- Aged51a's K02 identity conflicts with parent run51 K01. No confident correction can be made from the workbook alone.

## Which measurements can be harmonized and which cannot?

### Takeaway
Control units and combined ISS scatter voltage are already harmonized by the source workbook. The analogous STS detector column has documented not-used/zero records and cannot be naively pooled. Numeric zero, missing, saturation and detection limits require separate statuses.

### Cited Findings
- Combined fields A campaign (`1` SAME,`2` SAME-R), C material, D sample ID, E test identifier,G SAME run ID,B carousel,F carousel position,I GMT,J date. AW ISS detector scatter V and AX STS detector V are measured source-reported analog outputs; AY STS offset V. AV ISS obscuration V. No raw detector signal is an eligible input to condition→detector-label learning. — [Workbook](https://psi.nasa.gov/geode-py/ws/studies/PSI-101/download?file=PSI-101_Analyzed%20Data_SAME%2C%20SAME-R_Results.xlsx&version=4&redirect=false)
- AW is numeric in all154 recognized flight rows. Primary SAME range0.0006866452–6.2939V; SAME-R0.1842–6.283677V. Many values cluster near6.25V, so quantitative regression of large voltages risks saturation censoring. If independently validated published2V alarm criterion is used, saturation above2V does not destroy the positive binary label. Primary SAME labels at2V:13 above,4 below; SAME-R48 above,19 below. — [Workbook](https://psi.nasa.gov/geode-py/ws/studies/PSI-101/download?file=PSI-101_Analyzed%20Data_SAME%2C%20SAME-R_Results.xlsx&version=4&redirect=false)
- Source SAME-R sheet `SAME R Results` includes `Use STS Detector` colU, often `n`, with AS STS detector0 and AT offset0. SAME has near-negative-zero STS signals in some observations. These are not defensible no-detect labels without operation/background checks. Do not substitute0 for missing. — [Workbook](https://psi.nasa.gov/geode-py/ws/studies/PSI-101/download?file=PSI-101_Analyzed%20Data_SAME%2C%20SAME-R_Results.xlsx&version=4&redirect=false)
- BL M0 number/cm3 (unit verified in flight-specific sheet30 BD and31 AK), BM M1 mm/cm3, BQ calibrated/dilution-corrected DustTrak B mg/m3. BR AMD µm is deterministic1000*M1/M0, BS diameter-average-mass µm, BU/BV lognormal Hatch-Choate sigma/geometric diameter. BW/BX/BY CPC size-dependent calibration counts. Source reports zero-filled moment-derived quantities for DBP even when positive raw CPC is present; do not treat these as physical zero moments. Mark suspect/unsupported derived zeros as invalid. Text markers include NA,n/a,??,?, Excel errors, blanks. — [Workbook](https://psi.nasa.gov/geode-py/ws/studies/PSI-101/download?file=PSI-101_Analyzed%20Data_SAME%2C%20SAME-R_Results.xlsx&version=4&redirect=false)
- SAME-R added MPASS. Combined BN/BO are MPASS-specific and unavailable for SAME, so not cross-campaign harmonized. CB DustTrak material-specific TEOM calibration factor, CC dilution-related factor, CD density and CE derived temperature are source analysis outputs; their interpretation requires underlying calibrations, and they must not be reapplied to already-corrected data. Raw STS signals, instrument gains, MPASS moments and TEM morphological summaries are not all instrument-equivalent across campaigns. — [Workbook](https://psi.nasa.gov/geode-py/ws/studies/PSI-101/download?file=PSI-101_Analyzed%20Data_SAME%2C%20SAME-R_Results.xlsx&version=4&redirect=false)

### Inferences
- A derived binary2V response is defensible only after reference verification of the threshold/voltage convention; call it threshold response for this experiment, not operational ISS alarm or generalized safety.
- No extrapolation to unseen materials or actual spacecraft fire risk is justified. Validation should stress campaign shift and use repeated-sample groups.

### Gaps
- This audit does not independently reconstruct every raw calibration, exact per-observation saturation state, or electronic resolution. Do not invent thresholds for generic below-limit/saturation assignment. Preserve numeric voltage and state `saturation_not_individually_resolved` where applicable, using only threshold labels that remain identifiable.
- No human annotation is present; any labels generated by deterministic published-threshold application have provenance `derived`. Calibrated workbook measurements remain `source_reported`, with source-provided deterministic derived diameters explicitly distinguished.
